title: Two Grips, Each Wired to a Cable

scenes.tts: Take the calcium away from a sheet of cultured epithelial cells. They round up and let go of one another. Put it back, and they knit together again. What was the calcium holding? It stiffens the outer arms of adhesion proteins called cadherins, so one cell's arm can grip the next.
scenes.visual: A row of cells loses its calcium dots and the cells round up and part; calcium returns and they rejoin; zoom to one junction where limp cadherin arms stiffen with calcium at their joints and meet.
scenes.narration: Take the calcium away from a sheet of cultured epithelial cells. They round up and let go of one another. Put it back, and they knit together again. What was the calcium holding? It stiffens the outer arms of adhesion proteins called cadherins, so one cell's arm can grip the next.

scenes.tts: A cadherin crosses the membrane once. Its outer arm binds the same kind of cadherin on the next cell. Inside, beta-catenin binds the tail directly and recruits alpha-catenin, which couples the junction to actin filaments. A third protein, p one twenty catenin, binds the tail near the membrane. So a pull on the outside reaches the cell's own filaments.

scenes.visual: The junction builds the chain cadherin, beta-catenin, alpha-catenin, actin on both cells; p120 sits by the tail; a pull on one cell sends a pulse down the chain.

scenes.tts: The second grip is on the extracellular matrix, the woven material cells secrete around themselves. The main matrix receptors are integrins, each pairing one alpha subunit with one beta subunit. Mammals have eighteen alpha and eight beta subunits, which pair into twenty-four different integrins. Many recognise a short sequence, R G D, found in fibronectin. Inside, talin binds the beta tail and links it to actin, and vinculin reinforces the link.
scenes.caption: The second grip is on the extracellular matrix, the woven material cells secrete around themselves. The main matrix receptors are integrins, each pairing one α subunit with one β subunit. Mammals have 18 α and 8 β subunits, which pair into 24 different integrins. Many recognise a short sequence, RGD, found in fibronectin. Inside, talin binds the β tail and links it to actin, and vinculin reinforces the link.
scenes.visual: A cell sits on a matrix mesh; an integrin made of an alpha and a beta lobe grips the RGD tag on fibronectin; talin links it to an actin cable and vinculin reinforces the link.

scenes.tts: Not every integrin reaches actin. Hemidesmosomes pin the basal cells of skin to their basement membrane. There, integrin alpha six beta four binds laminin three three two outside the cell. It connects through plectin to keratin filaments. Two chains with the same overall shape end on different cables.

scenes.visual: The actin chain slides left; a second integrin chain appears on the right, binding laminin in the basement membrane and ending on a keratin cable through plectin.

scenes.tts: A cell pulls on its adhesions with myosin two. Do the links themselves respond? A purified talin rod is a stack of thirteen helical bundles. Stretched at twelve piconewtons, it showed more vinculin binding events, from one at most to as many as three. The reading is that force unfolds bundles and exposes vinculin sites hidden inside them.
scenes.caption: A cell pulls on its adhesions with myosin II. Do the links themselves respond? A purified talin rod is a stack of 13 helical bundles. scenes.visual: Myosin pulls the actin of the chain; the talin chip becomes a row of 13 bundles; pulled at 12 pN, the binding-event count goes from at most 1 to 3; three bundles unfold and vinculin heads bind the exposed sites.

scenes.tts: Autoinhibition is the folded-shut state that hides a protein's binding sites. In mouse fibroblasts, releasing it let talin and vinculin associate, even with myosin two blocked. Purified fragments show that force can expose sites. A cell assay shows that activation can do it without force. Keep the systems apart, because neither says which route dominates in a tissue.
